solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ned, joining pals assembling inside, looks for stairs in east London

indicators.note: inside says the shuffled letters go within the word for looks

parts.note: looks, as in seems, means appears

indicators.note: assembling means putting the letters of Ned and pals together in a new order

explanation.surface: Ned joins his friends gathering indoors and searches for a staircase in the East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' is only a link. Cockney rhyming slang, from London's East End, uses this phrase to mean stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang: the phrase rhymes with the word for a flight of steps.

clue.text: Judy's partner at front of ship, left vessel

parts.note: in the traditional Punch and Judy puppet show, Judy's husband is Punch
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A puppet's mate stands at the ship's prow and then departs a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bowl for serving a mixed drink is a vessel in the sense of a container.

clue.text: Say party line, upsetting group of masons

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the whole run of pieces upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: say, meaning for example, gives EG
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone toes a political party line and causes upset among freemasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in local branches, each called by this word for a chapter of the order.

clue.text: One leaves sandwiches to grab auntie regularly distributing wine

indicators.note: to grab means the trimmed sandwich word takes hold of other letters inside it
leaves means the letter for one departs from the sandwich word

parts.note: sarnies is British slang for sandwiches
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: regularly distributing means only every other letter of auntie is handed out

explanation.surface: A relative grabs sandwiches and hands out drink at a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarnies is everyday British slang for sandwiches; 'regularly distributing' takes the even letters of auntie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France, named after its village.

clue.text: Bottom drain repaired

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters of drain are fixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The lowest point of a drain has been fixed by a plumber.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of something, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: Strain spread around royal column

indicators.note: around means the word for spread goes round the other pieces

parts.note: pate, a meat paste, is a spread
ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is a crossword stand-in for royal

explanation.surface: Something smeared around a stately pillar is being filtered.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain a liquid is to let it seep through a filter, as coffee does.

clue.text: China's major highway blocked earlier

indicators.note: blocked means the word for earlier is obstructed by something set inside it

parts.note: ago means earlier, in the past
the M1 is Britain's major motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A Chinese motorway was jammed some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: China means friend from Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate). The M1 is England's main north-south motorway, its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: China is rhyming slang for mate, and this Spanish word means friend.

clue.text: Staff threat, as numbers two and four are exchanged

indicators.text: numbers two and four are exchanged
indicators.note: the second and fourth letters of the word for threat trade places

parts.note: a spectre is a looming threat

explanation.surface: Staff are threatened when the second and fourth numbers in a list are swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: In SPECTRE the second letter P and fourth letter C swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial rod carried by a monarch is a staff of office.

clue.text: Horses attract the eye of bookmaker, making new book

indicators.note: attract means the horses draw another letter in among them

parts.note: roans are horses with mixed-colour coats

indicators.note: the eye of a word is its centre letter

explanation.surface: Horses catch a bookie's attention and he opens a fresh betting book.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the nine-letter bookmaker is M; it goes inside ROANS. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Romans is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Had particular boundaries in England

parts.note: own means particular, as in one's own room

indicators.note: boundaries are the outermost letters of a word

explanation.surface: England once had its own distinct borders.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to possess it, so the past tense means possessed.

clue.text: Second-in-command, no good against Spain, shows stress

indicators.note: no means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: an underling is a subordinate
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A deputy playing badly against Spain shows signs of strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link word; the definition is the verb stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to draw a line under it figuratively.

clue.text: American allowed to wear the jumper?

indicators.note: to wear means the word for allowed is clothed by the next word, sitting inside it

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: An American is permitted to put on a woolly sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater, which the surface encourages, but it means a high or long jumper in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A high jumper or long jumper is a sportsperson in track and field.

clue.text: Completely remove bounder seen by all in shot

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, bounds along

indicators.note: in means the letter for all goes inside the word for shot

parts.note: a tot is a small shot of spirits
U is the film rating meaning suitable for all

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a cad who has been spotted by everyone in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' suggests a cad, but here it is a kangaroo. U is the British film certificate for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something out by the roots is to eradicate it entirely.

clue.text: "Poorly" mainly coming across to patient

indicators.note: coming across means the trimmed word for poorly spans the other piece
mainly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: sick means poorly, unwell

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly comes over to a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like a noun, a person in hospital, but it is the adjective meaning long-suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who endures hardship calmly without complaint, like the ancient philosophers.

clue.text: Ketchup perhaps appearing thick inside American bread

indicators.note: inside means these pieces are set within the American money word

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and a cent is American money
on means appearing, as a performer on stage
dim means thick, stupid

explanation.surface: A tomato sauce shows up as something thick inside a loaf of American bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketchup is an example of a sauce or seasoning added to food.

clue.text: Single figure picks up crate to distribute fruit

indicators.note: picks up means the number word takes in the other letters

parts.note: nine is a single-digit figure

indicators.note: to distribute means the letters of crate are spread in a new order

explanation.surface: One person lifts a crate in order to hand out fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single figure' looks like a lone person, but it means a one-digit number.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a stone fruit.

clue.text: Domestic garland coated gold, boosting Belgian place

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, a domestic

indicators.note: coated means the garland covers the gold, enclosing it

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland

indicators.note: boosting means raising, so in a down clue gold reads upwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A housekeeper's flower wreath is gilded to lift a Belgian town's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'boosting' lifts gold so it reads upwards. A char is a British word for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the Wallonia region of Belgium.

clue.text: One quietly gatecrashes military fair

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: gatecrashes means the letter for quietly forces its way inside

parts.note: martial means military
p, for piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone quietly slips uninvited into an army fete.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair judge is unbiased, treating all sides alike.

clue.text: Antipodeans around here heard parrot flapping in sea

indicators.note: heard means the parrot's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Polly is the stock name for a pet parrot

indicators.note: flapping means the letters of in and sea are agitated into new order

explanation.surface: Australians nearby heard a parrot beating its wings over the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives POLY for Polly; 'flapping' rearranges IN SEA as NESIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This group of Pacific islands lies on the far side of the world from Britain, near Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Controversial photo captures expression of victory by metres

indicators.note: captures means the photo word holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
ole is the cry of triumph at a bullfight or football match
M is the abbreviation for metres

explanation.surface: A photograph catches a cheer at a winning margin of metres.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, the word describes argumentative, disputatious writing or speech.

clue.text: Free invite excludes frst year

indicators.note: excludes first (misprinted frst) means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to tempt is to invite or entice

explanation.surface: An invitation that leaves out the first year of a course is free of charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty means unoccupied, vacant, as a free seat is.

clue.text: Snooker ball forming line, see, in wooden frame

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the word for the wood

parts.note: yew is a wood used for frames such as longbows
lo is an old word meaning see, look

explanation.surface: Snooker balls form a line inside a wooden triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming' is a link. Snooker has one ball of each colour besides the reds.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, one of the coloured balls, worth two points.

clue.text: Meadow and wood keep end of village more rural

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: keep means the wood holds the next letter inside

parts.note: fir is a wood

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of village

explanation.surface: Meadows and woodland preserve the edge of a village as countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Having more leaves suggests greener, more countrified surroundings.

clue.text: Tree ring follows annual succession, primarily

indicators.note: follows means the word for ring comes after the first pieces
primarily picks the first letters of annual and succession

parts.note: a pen or ring is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Tree rings show yearly growth when studied first.
explanation.definitionFit: A poplar with trembling leaves is a type of tree.

clue.text: Bar popular French artist manually

parts.note: a rod is a bar
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A bar popular with French artists who work by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manually' closes the clue as a hint: the sculptor modelled his works by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin, the French sculptor of The Thinker.

clue.text: Some claret almost knocked over sideways

indicators.note: knocked over means the run of letters is turned to read backwards
some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A glass of claret was nearly knocked over sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside claret almost lies LARETAL, which 'knocked over' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means to the side, so it matches sideways.

clue.text: Body fat's latest reading — approximately

indicators.note: latest picks the last letter of fat's

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: A body fat measurement gives only a rough figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Mother, prepared when travelling, cut out page for navigator

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: when travelling means the letters of prepared move around
cut out means the letter for page is taken away from the mix

explanation.surface: Mum, all set for a journey, removes a page from the road atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when travelling' scrambles prepared, and 'cut out' drops one of its two P's.
explanation.definitionFit: The passenger who follows the route on a map guides the driver.

clue.text: Greek character carries home animal

indicators.note: carries means the Greek letter holds the word for home within it

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
in means at home

explanation.surface: A character in a Greek play brings home a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A large horned mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Fixed work, in building line, means capital no longer used

parts.note: constant means fixed, unchanging

indicators.note: in means the word for work goes inside the shuffled line
building means the letters of line are constructed in a new arrangement

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Steady work on a building line means a capital no longer in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is a link. The city was renamed Istanbul in 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of Istanbul, Ottoman and Byzantine capital, is no longer in use.
